subject: Order Form timing: aligning notice windows & termination-for-convenience language
messages:
From: LumenHealth Procurement <procurement@lumenhealth.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com
Cc: sara.ong@lumenhealth.com
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Order Form: notice window and TfC questions

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week — LumenHealth is excited by the perf and observability. Legal asked us to double-check two items in the draft order form / MSA bundle you shared:

1) Auto-renew notice window: the draft suggests a 60-day notice period before renewal. Procurement would prefer a 30-day notice so our budget team can decide before the next quarter. Can Redwood accommodate 30 days (or a staggered 45/30 option)?

2) Termination for Convenience (TfC): Lumen legal is pushing for a 30-day TfC right with a pro-rated refund of unused prepaid committed capacity. Your current MSA shows 90 days and limited refund language. Can we get a middle ground?

We attached the redlines Lumen proposed (see LumenHealth_Draft_Redlines_20271129.pdf). Please advise on Redwood's flexibility and next steps for legal redlines coordination.

Time is a bit tight — looking to finalize by Dec 3. Happy to loop in your legal if useful.

Thanks,
Procurement Team
LumenHealth

Attachment: LumenHealth_Draft_Redlines_20271129.pdf (PDF, 1 page summary)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: LumenHealth Procurement <procurement@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: sara.ong@lumenhealth.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: notice window and TfC questions

Hi — thanks for the clear ask and for flagging the attached redlines. I reviewed with Product and Legal, and proposing the path below to try to close by Dec 3: 

- Notice window: we can reduce to 45 days firm. As an alternative we can offer a 30-day option for pilot/tiered SKUs (we'd need to restrict to non-enterprise reserved commitments). If you can confirm which SKU the PO will reference, we can pick 45 vs. 30.

- TfC: Redwood is reluctant to move to a full 30-day TfC because of reserved capacity commitments on Dedicated pools. Proposed compromise: 60-day TfC with pro-rated refund of prepaid unused committed dollars minus a 10% reconfiguration fee (covers GPU reservation reallocation). This preserves continuity but reduces the risk on our side.

I've attached our suggested language as a doc (Redline_Suggested_TFC_v2.docx) and highlighted the notice options. If that looks OK, Karthish (copied) will run the exact MSA/order form redline and we can send a single consolidated package back to you.

If you prefer, we can do a 15-minute call today at 3pm PT to speed signoff.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redline_Suggested_TFC_v2.docx (Word, proposed clause), internal_notes.txt (internal only)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, LumenHealth Procurement <procurement@lumenhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form: notice window and TfC questions

Naomi — quick legal pass attached and inline notes below. I kept the tone pragmatic to avoid reopening broader MSA points. Key suggestions: 

- Notice window: Accept 45 days as standard; for 30 days we will require that customer does not purchase reserved Dedicated pools (i.e., hosted API or metered consumption only). I added a one-line definition to the Order Form to lock that dependency.

- TfC: Counterpropose 60-day TfC with pro-rata refund of unused prepayments "less costs reasonably incurred by Redwood to unwind reserved capacity and migration assistance". To keep it simple for procurement, I recommended capping recoverable costs at 15% (we proposed 10% earlier in Ops; Legal suggests 15% for margin). I've included bracketed language so you can choose 10% or 15% depending on negotiation appetite.

- Transition obligations: Add explicit 30-day offboarding support SLA after termination for convenience (export of logs, config handover). That tends to be a procurement ask and reduces churn for both sides.

Putting the clean marked-up Order Form into the thread now; Marissa, please confirm the pricing/sku note for 30-day option.

Karthik
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference

Attachment: RF_Redline_TfC_v1.pdf (redline with bracketed percentages)

Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 16:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Final: agreed notice window and TfC compromise + next steps

Hi Sara / Procurement team,

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Based on our internal alignment (legal + ops + pricing) and your timeline, here's what Redwood can sign today: 

1) Notice window: 45 days standard. If Lumen confirms the Order Form will reference metered/hosted SKUs only, we will accept 30 days (note must be explicit in the Order Form line item).

2) Tfc (Termination for Convenience): 60 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of unused prepaid committed amounts, less a 10% unwind fee. We've accepted the lower 10% ops proposal to keep this moving.

3) Transition support: Redwood will provide 30 days of offboarding support (export assistance, access handover documentation, and one senior engineer checkpoint).

Next steps:
- I'll attach a clean Order Form with the redline accepted and e-sign package to follow.
- Please confirm the SKU type (metered/hosted vs reserved/dedicated) by EOD Dec 2 so we can lock the notice window.

DocuSign link: https://naomi.redwoodinference.com/docusign/LH-0912
HubSpot opp: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/opp/HO-98765

If you want a quick call, I'm free tomorrow morning PST. Otherwise we'll send the consolidated MSA + Order Form for signature once you confirm SKU.

Best regards,
Naomi Feldman

Redwood Inference
